cases.headline: APLAPOLLO is crashing hard, but the bars swing too wildly for a tight stop and the move looks stretched, so we stay out.
cases.bull:
Honest long case: this is a mean-reversion bounce, and it's weak.

Setup: APLAPOLLO fell from ~2121 (Nov 20 close) to 1670 yesterday, a 21% drop in one session on 26.1M shares versus a 2.2M 20-day average. Today it opened at 1503 (the data shows a -10% gap vs 1670 close, though the "gap" stat reads -0.1) and printed 1419.5, roughly 33% below the 20-day high of 2312. That is extreme, capitulation-style selling with relvol 65x. Sharp exhaustion can produce a snap-back toward VWAP 1431 and the 1451 mid-bar.

Entry: only on a reclaim, not now. Buy a 5-minute close back above VWAP ~1431, ideally after a higher low above 1419.5. Stop: just under 1419.5, say 1412, risking ~19 points. Target: 1451-1455 (the 09:20 close and 09:25 open), about 1:1.5 at best. A stretch is 1475.

What proves me wrong: any trade below 1419.5, since the last bar closed on its low (1419.5) with 3.66M volume, the heaviest of the day, and the stock sits at its low, 0.5% below nothing to support it. Index is up 0.47% and the stock still falls, which is bad relative strength. Honestly, there's no confirmation, and costs eat a marginal bounce. I'd lean pass.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The Bull's bounce thesis needs a reclaim above VWAP 1431.13, but the last bar closed at 1419.5, the day low, 11.6 points below VWAP, so no reclaim exists. A 1412 stop risks about 7.5 points with a 1451 target; after slippage of 0.05% (~0.7 points each way), that is thin. The "capitulation" claim isn't proven: the 09:25 bar's volume of 3.66M was double the prior bar's 1.75M, so selling is accelerating, not fading. Index up 0.47% confirms relative weakness.

Short case: the stock is in a clear downtrend (5-day return -25.8%, price 1419.5 vs 20-day average 2155). Yesterday's session never bounced: it opened 1957.6 and closed 1670, near the low of 1650. Today's open at 1503 was the high, and each bar made lower lows.

Honest caveat: the stock is 15% below yesterday's low of 1650 and 1.9 times the daily ATR (86.6) beyond it, so extension risk is real. Stop 1503 is 84.5 points away; the Rs 500 risk allows only ~5 shares. The 1250 target is 169 points away, unrealistic.

Plan: short on a break below 1418.79, stop 1445 (above the 09:25 bar's high of 1455 is too wide; a VWAP reclaim invalidates it), target 1380. Otherwise stay out.

judge.title: No trade: Collapse is real, but the risk can't be sized: pass
judge.text: The short case is genuine: the stock gapped from 1670 to 1503, closed the 09:25 bar on its low at 1419.5 with 3.66M shares (double the prior bar), sits below VWAP 1431.13 and is falling while the index is up 0.47%. Against that, today's range is already 83.5 points, close to the daily ATR of 86.6. Price is about 15% below yesterday's low of 1650, after a -25.8% 5-day move on 26.1M shares versus a 2.2M average, which leaves a high risk of a violent snap-back. The tightest valid stop, 1445, is about 26 points, smaller than either 5-minute bar so far (64 and 36 points), and my record shows tight stops on similar shorts losing about -1.2R three times out of n=5. The rule's 1503 stop is too wide to reach its 1250 target before the close, so I pass and log the bear's short levels (1418.79 / 1445 / 1375) for scoring.

cases.headline: BRIGADE gapped above its 20-day high on heavy volume; buy only if it breaks 618.3, with a tighter stop.
cases.bull:
The case for long: BRIGADE gapped up 3.1% (open 601.15 vs prev close 583.0) and cleared the 20-day high of 583.9 immediately. It sits at 617.8, about 5.8% above that level. The three bars show steady buying: closes of 610.75, 613.9 and 617.8, with higher lows (600.5, 609.75, 611.5). Price is above VWAP (613.52), and the index is up 0.47%. Relative volume of 54.9x says this is real participation, not a drift. The first bar's 401,590 shares alone exceed the 20-day average daily volume of 396,280.

Entry: a buy-stop at 618.31, just above the OR high of 618.0. Don't chase before that. The plan's stop at 600.5 is far too wide: 17.8 points, about 2.2 ATR5, and it risks 2.9%. At Rs 500 risk that is only about 28 shares, so the position is small. A tighter stop near 611 (under the third bar's low of 611.5 and VWAP) would risk about 7 points, roughly 70 shares, which is more sensible.

Target: the plan's 653.93 equals 2R off the wide stop and is a stretch. Daily ATR is 19.63, so a realistic target is about 635 to 640, roughly one daily ATR above the OR high.

Wrong if: price closes a 5-minute bar back below VWAP or 611, or the breakout fails and returns inside the range. Also note the stock is already about 12% above its 20-day average (dma20 550.45), so it is extended, and the edge is modest after costs.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The gap is real, but 3.1% is a gap of only about 0.9 daily ATR (18.15 points vs ATR 19.63), so it is not extreme. Still, a gap that far above the 583.9 high is stretched, and the Bull concedes price is 12% above the 20-day average. "Higher lows" are weak evidence from three bars. Volume is fading each bar: 401,590, then 303,430, then 233,313, a 42% drop, while price grinds into the OR high. The 54.9x relvol is flattered by a thin early-session baseline, and the first bar contains the gap's opening burst. Price at 617.8 sits only 4.3 above VWAP, so the VWAP stop of ~611 is within noise (ATR5 8.2). Seventy shares at ~Rs 618 is about Rs 43k, so costs eat the thin edge.

Bear case: A failed breakout at 618.0, the third bar's high, is plausible. The stock rose 7.3% in five days and 3.1% on the gap, and the setup is exhausted. But this stock is outside F&O, so a short is not allowed. That settles the short side.

Verdict: no short. Stay out, or pass. If anyone insists on long, require a 5-minute close above 618.31 with volume holding above ~230k. Otherwise the edge after costs is marginal.

judge.title: BRIGADE: buy the opening-range breakout with a tightened stop
judge.text: The long case is stronger. The stock opened 3.1% up at 601.15, above the 20-day high of 583.9. Every 5-minute bar closed higher (610.75, 613.9, 617.8). Price is above VWAP at 613.52, the index is up 0.47%, and the first bar alone traded 401,590 shares, more than the 20-day average daily volume of 396,280. The Bear's points are fair: bar volume fell from 401k to 233k, and the stock is about 12% above its 20-day average after a 7.3% five-day run. Since a short is not allowed outside F&O, the only question is whether the long pays after costs. The plan's 600.5 stop is too far at 2.9% from the trigger, outside the 2% limit, so I use 609.5, just under the second bar's low of 609.75. That risks about 8.8 points, roughly one ATR5 of 8.23. The target of 632.5 is about 1.6R and about 0.7 daily ATR above the trigger, more reachable than 653.9. Conviction is only 3 because the volume is fading and the stock is extended, but entering only on a stop order above 618.31 means a failed breakout never fills.

cases.headline: NH is breaking to a new 20-day high on huge volume; take a small long on a push above 2064.5 with a stop under VWAP.
cases.bull:
**Case for the long:** NH is breaking out of a multi-week uptrend, and the first three bars show real buying. It gapped up 1.24% and rose 3.15%, closing at 2062.5, essentially the OR high of 2063.0. Each 5-minute bar made a higher low (1998.5, 2027, 2041.8) and a higher close. Price is above VWAP (2047.6). Today's high of 2063 also clears yesterday's high (1988.9) and the 20-day high (1992), and the index is up 0.47%. Relvol of 13x, with 176k shares in 15 minutes against a 20-day average daily volume of about 207k, is real participation. It follows the 784k-share breakout day on 11/20.

**Entry and stop:** Enter on a break of 2064, as the plan says. The plan's stop at 1998.5 is 65 points away, so a Rs 500 risk allows only 7 shares (about Rs 14k). A tighter stop just under VWAP, around 2040, is more practical, giving a risk of about 24 points. I'd prefer that.

**Target:** The plan's 2195 is too ambitious. A realistic goal is 2110-2125, roughly 1.5 daily ATR-equivalents of 30 per 5 bars, or about 2R from the tighter stop.

**Proof I'm wrong:** A close back below VWAP, or a failed break that falls back under 2040. A price already 3% up and 12% above its 20-day average could also simply exhaust itself.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: the Bull's points are mostly accurate, but they weaken the case. Volume is flat to fading across the bars (57k, 60k, 58k), not building. The stock is already up 3.15% and has run 6.2% from yesterday's close 1975 to 2062.5, which is about 1.7x the daily ATR of 50.49. It sits 12% above the 20-day average (1846.59). Buying a break of 2064 means entering after the move is spent. The Bull's 2040 stop is also not safe: bar 3 alone ranged 21 points (ATR5 is 30), so a 24-point stop is within normal noise, and slippage is about 4 points. Entering at 2064 and stopping at 2040 leaves a risk of about 28 points after costs, and a 2110-2125 target is only 1.6-2.2R. That's thin.

Short case: this is a Nifty-type tape, not a bearish one, and the index is up 0.47%. Shorting is not allowed anyway (outside F&O, long only). So the honest answer is to stay out unless the long is cleaner.

No short trigger. If forced, the only acceptable long is a pullback to VWAP near 2048 that holds, with a stop under 2030 and a target at 2110. Otherwise, pass.

judge.title: NH: momentum breakout long, tight stop under VWAP
judge.text: The deciding facts favour the long. Relative volume is 13x, with about 176k shares traded in 15 minutes against a 207k daily average. Price closed the opening range at 2062.5, right at the 2063 high, with three higher lows (1998.5, 2027, 2041.8). Today's high also clears the 20-day high of 1992, two sessions after the 784k-share breakout day of 11/20, and the index is up 0.47%. The Bear is right that the move is stretched: 87.5 points from the 1975 close is about 1.7x the 50.49 daily ATR, and volume is flat (57k/60k/58k), not building. That is why conviction is only 2 and the target is a modest 2110 (about 1.9R), not the plan's 2195. The stop at 2040 sits below VWAP (2047.6) and below the third bar's low, giving 24.5 points of risk, about 20 shares for Rs 500. This is a long-only name outside F&O, and my small sample (n=11 refused rule trades averaging +0.10R, vs +0.24R for the rule plan over n=17) argues mildly against sitting out clean momentum setups.

cases.headline: SOBHA is pressing its opening high on heavy volume; buy only if it breaks 1280.5, with a modest target below last week's 1308 ceiling.
cases.bull:
Case for long: SOBHA closed the opening range at 1278.1, within 0.14% of the OR high (1279.9), and above VWAP (1270.1). Relative volume is 6.4x. Bars 2 and 3 carried 13,379 and 11,151 shares, versus 5,820 in yesterday's first 15 minutes. The stock gapped up 0.71% over yesterday's high of 1271.2 and is up 1.44% on a day when the index is up 0.47%, so it is beating the market. Higher lows (1256.3, 1256.8, 1264.1) show buyers stepping in. The 20-day return is +6.6% and the price is well above the 20DMA (1224.3).

Entry: a buy-stop at about 1280.5, only on a real break of the OR high with volume. Chasing at 1278 is acceptable but gives less confirmation.

Stop: the plan's 1256.3 is 24 points away, about 2x ATR5, so size must be small (about 20 shares for Rs 500). A tighter stop under 1264 (the last bar's low) is about 16 points away and still sits below the structure.

Target: the plan's 1329 is too ambitious. It sits near the 20-day high of 1329.9. A realistic target is 1305-1310, near the 11/13 high of 1308, which is about 1.5R.

Proven wrong: a close back below VWAP (~1270), or a failed break that falls under 1264.

Caveat: the 14-day daily ATR is 48, so the stock reverses a lot. Costs eat a marginal edge.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: The Bull's volume comparison is apples to oranges. Today's 13,379 and 11,151 are 5-minute bars; yesterday's 5,820 was a 15-minute bar. The Bull's "higher lows" come from three bars, and the first bar's 2,610 shares shows a thin start. Relative volume of 6.4x is real, but it comes from a stock averaging 172k shares/day, and 15 minutes of 27k shares is small. The 1.44% move versus the index's 0.47% is only a 1% edge, well inside a daily ATR of 48 (3.8%). The Bull's tighter stop under 1264 is only 16 points, about 1.4x ATR5, so noise can easily hit it.

Bear case: The last bar spiked 15 points (1264.1 to 1279.9) and closed at 1278.1, about 8 points above VWAP, so entry is extended. The daily bars show repeated failures at the 1308-1317 area (11/13, 11/17), and the stock closed back near 1251-1270 each time. Yesterday it faded from a 1271.2 high to 1251.1. The 5-day return is flat (-0.02%), so the 20-day strength has stalled. SOBHA is non-F&O, so a short can't be traded.

Verdict: stay out. Long is marginal after costs (about 25% of risk). Only consider a long on a volume-backed break above 1280.5, stop 1264, target 1305.

judge.title: SOBHA: small long on a confirmed opening-range break, tight structure stop
judge.text: The stock is pressing the opening-range high, and the Bull's evidence for that holds up: price is 1278.1, just 0.14% under the 1279.9 OR high and about 8 points above VWAP (1270.1). Relative volume is 6.4x, the gap took it above yesterday's 1271.2 high, and it is up 1.44% against the index's 0.47%. The Bear is right that the 1308-1317 zone capped both 11/13 and 11/17, and that the 5-day return is flat at -0.02%, so the plan's 1329 target is unrealistic. I therefore use 1306, just below 1308, and a stop under the 1264.1 last-bar low. That gives 16.5 points of risk (1.29%) against 25.5 points of reward, about 1.55R, which still leaves room after the 0.2% slippage. Conviction stays at 2 because the edge is thin, the daily ATR of 48 means wide swings, and my record is too small to lean on (n=11 refused rule trades averaged +0.10R; the rule plan averaged +0.24R over 17 fills).

cases.headline: IndusInd Bank is giving back yesterday's surge on heavy selling, so short a break below today's low with a tight stop above the average price.
cases.bull:
Honest case for a long here is weak, and I'd say so up front. The only real argument is a mean-reversion bounce: price fell 2.7% in 20 minutes (1001.4 to 974.15) on 4.38x relative volume, and the last bar closed on the low, 0.0002 below the OR low of 974.3. Stretched intraday moves often retrace toward VWAP (984.09), about 10 points or roughly 1 ATR (11.04) above.

Entry: only after a failed breakdown, meaning a 5-minute close back above 974.3 (the OR low) with the bar after it holding. Stop just under the day low, around 972.5, so risk is about 2-3 points. Target: VWAP at ~984, a 9-11 point gain, roughly 3-4R on paper. Realistically take it there, not at the scanner's far-off 914.

Caveats: the 09:30 bar had only 36k volume, probably incomplete, so it proves little. The index is down 0.93%, and every bar so far made lower lows and closed lower. Costs eat a quarter of risk, and a tight stop gets clipped easily.

Wrong if: price closes below 974.15 again, or any bounce stalls under 980.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The bounce thesis is thin, as the Bull admits. Relative volume of 4.38x with a 2.7% drop is evidence of selling pressure, not exhaustion. Every bar made lower highs and lower lows, closing 996.95, 982.3, 977.7, 974.15. VWAP at 984 is only a target if price bounces, and nothing shows it will. The Bull's 2-3 point stop is under 0.3 ATR (11.04), and costs are a quarter of risk, so it would be clipped by noise. The 3-4R claim is paper only.

Short case: the index is down 0.93%, so the weakness is confirmed, and price sits at the OR low (974.3) with no bounce. The 09:30 bar is incomplete (36k volume), so a close below 974.15 matters.

Against shorting: price is already 1 ATR below VWAP, and the scanner's stop at 1003.45 is 29 points away (about 2.7 ATR), while its 914 target is 60 points away. That is too wide for Rs 500 risk, sizing roughly 16 shares. Yesterday's low (906) is far below, so there is no nearby support, but chasing a 2.7% extended move is poor.

Verdict: stay out unless a pullback to about 981-984 fails. Then short ~982, stop 987, target 970. Otherwise no trade.

judge.title: Short INDUSINDBK on OR-low break, stop above VWAP
judge.text: The stock has fallen 2.7% from the 1001.4 open to 974.15 on 4.38x relative volume, with four straight lower closes (996.95, 982.3, 977.7, 974.15). The Nifty is also down 0.93%, so this is confirmed selling and not a stock-specific blip; the Bull's bounce case has no reversal bar to stand on. Yesterday's 906–1003 range means there is little support until the low 950s. I reject the scanner's 1003.45 stop because it is about 3% away, outside the 2% limit and too wide for Rs 500 of risk; I use 985.0 instead, just above VWAP at 984.09 and about 1 ATR (11.04) from entry, and target 955.5 for roughly 1.6R. Conviction is only 2 because price is already a full ATR below VWAP. The 09:30 bar is thin at 36k shares, and my similar past shorts were marginal, so a snap-back toward 984 is a real risk.

cases.headline: Axis Bank is falling hard with the market; a small short only if it breaks to a new low under 1405.7.
cases.bull:
Honest case for a long is thin, and I'd call it a countertrend bounce at best.

The argument: AXISBANK has fallen 3.0% from the 1452.5 open to 1408.8, and sits just 0.17% above the opening-range low of 1406.4. That is stretched against ATR5 of 14.1: price is about 10.4 points (0.7 ATR) under VWAP of 1419.2 after a 51-point range collapse in 15 minutes. The last bar (09:30) held 1408.8 on volume of 68k, down sharply from 563k and 434k, so selling is fading. Daily trend is up, with prev_low 1368.8 and the 20DMA at 1290.

Entry: only on a reclaim, e.g. a 5-minute close above 1413, with the 1406.4 low intact. Stop: below 1405, about 8 points of risk, so roughly 60 shares for Rs 500. Target: VWAP at ~1419, roughly 1.3R, and a stretch to 1430 only if volume returns.

Wrong if: price breaks 1406.4 on rising volume (relvol is 4.3, so sellers are active), or the index (-0.9%) keeps sliding. Gross edge is small after costs, so I'd pass without the reclaim.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: The Bull's "fading selling" rests on one bar, and the 09:30 bar is likely incomplete or just a pause; 68k against 563k tells us little. Price closed at 1408.8, the bar's low, so sellers still won that bar. The 0.7 ATR gap under VWAP (10.4 points) is not stretched; a 51-point collapse that holds near the low is trend, not exhaustion. The long needs a close above 1413 to even start, so the bounce is hypothetical. Targeting VWAP at 1419 gives about 1.3R, which costs at a quarter of risk shrink to roughly 1R. The index at -0.9% also argues against fading the move.

Short case: it is real but late. Price sits 2.4 points above the OR low, and a break at 1405.7 would be a fresh low on a down day. However, the plan's stop at 1448 is 42 points (3 ATR) away, and the 1321 target is 85 points below, which is unrealistic for one session. Risk of 42 points means about 12 shares, so the size is tiny.

My plan: short only on a 5-minute close below 1405.7 with volume above the 68k bar. Stop 1419.5, just above VWAP (about 14 points). Target 1385, about 1.5R. Otherwise stay out; the chase is poor.

judge.title: AXISBANK: late but valid opening-range-low break, tight stop above VWAP
judge.text: Price is down 3.0% from the 1452.5 open, sits only 2.4 points above the 1406.4 range low, and trades about 10 points under VWAP of 1419.2. Volume is 4.3x normal and the index is down 0.9%, so the trend and the market both favour the short side. The Bull's fading-volume point rests on one partial 68k bar that still closed at its low (1408.8), and the long needs a reclaim that has not happened. I take the Bear's tighter plan rather than the rule plan: the rule's 42-point stop and 1321 target are unrealistic. Conviction stays at 2 because the stock has already fallen about 3.6 ATR (51 points against an ATR of 14.1) in 15 minutes, so a snap-back is a real risk. The stop at 1419.5 sits just above VWAP (13.8 points of risk), and the 1384.5 target is about 1.5R; my record of 4 wrong no-trades out of 10 (n=18 calls, weak evidence) argues against sitting this one out.

cases.headline: Canara Bank has already fallen about 3% this morning and sits just above yesterday's low, so shorting now chases the move. Stay out.
cases.bull:
Honest read: the long case is weak, and I'd say so up front.

The bull argument is a mean-reversion bounce, not a breakout. CANBK sits at 135.52, just 0.19% above the opening-range low of 135.26, after falling 2.96% from the 140.3 high. Prior-day low is 134.15, and the stock is well above its 20-DMA of 125.29, so the higher-timeframe trend is up. The last bar (09:30) printed on only 188k shares versus ~2M earlier, suggesting selling is fading, though that bar may simply be incomplete.

Entry: only on a reclaim, say a 5-minute close above VWAP 136.73, confirming buyers. Stop: below the 135.26 day low, around 134.8 (about 1.9 risk, roughly 1.3 ATR). Target: 138.0, the first 5-min close area, about 1.3 reward, which is under 1:1 risk-reward.

Problems: price is below VWAP, the index is down 0.93%, relvol 3.89 confirms heavy selling, and three consecutive lower closes. Costs are about a quarter of risk, so a sub-1:1 bounce is negative expectancy.

Wrong if: price closes below 135.26. I'd pass on the long.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The bull's 20-DMA point (125.29) is daily context and says nothing about the next hour; price has already dropped 2.96% from the 140.3 high. The thin 09:30 bar (188k vs ~2M) is incomplete, as the bull concedes, so it proves nothing about fading sellers. The reclaim of VWAP 136.73 is a modest ask, but it needs about 1.2 points of upside and then gives sub-1:1 reward. I agree with the bull's pass on the long.

Short case: three straight lower closes (138.0, 136.47, 135.71), a lower high every bar, price under VWAP, index down 0.93%, and relvol 3.89. Sellers are in control.

Honest weaknesses: price is already at the OR low, so a short at 135.19 chases a move that is 2.96% done. Prior-day low 134.15 is only about 1 point below the trigger and is likely support. The plan's target of 126.27 is unrealistic, 9 points away or roughly 6 ATRs. The stop at 139.65 is 4.46 away, so sizing is tiny, and costs eat the edge.

If taking it: short on a 5-minute close below 135.19, stop 136.80 (just above VWAP), target 134.15 for a first scale-out, then 132.8 at most. Reward to 134.15 is only about 1.0 against 1.6 risk, so my honest lean is to stay out unless the break is clean on volume.

judge.title: No trade: CANBK: the short is real but late, with support close below
judge.text: The short case is real but late, so I am staying out. Sellers lead, with three lower closes (138.0, 136.47, 135.71), price at 135.52 under VWAP 136.73, relative volume 3.89x and the index down 0.93%. But the stock is already down 2.96% from 140.3 and sits 0.19% above the 135.26 opening-range low, and yesterday's low of 134.15 is only about 1 point below a 135.19 trigger, so it is likely to act as a floor. A sensible stop has to sit above the recent lower highs, near 136.45, about 1.26 points away, which needs a target of 133.30 for 1.5x. That target lies beyond the 134.15 support, and with costs at about a quarter of risk the edge is thin. The rule plan's 126.27 target (about 6 ATR away) and its 4.46-point stop are unrealistic, and both Bull and Bear leaned toward passing. My history of refused rule trades (+0.09R) and the scanner's record (+0.22R) rest on small samples (n=10 and n=13), so they do not outweigh today's poor entry location.

cases.headline: Adani Enterprises gave back its whole opening gap; sell only if it breaks below yesterday's close at about 2709.
cases.bull:
Honest case for a long is thin, but here it is.

Thesis: a failed breakdown/mean-reversion bounce. ADANIENT gapped up 1.38% (open 2746.3 vs prev close 2709.0), sold off to 2711.2 (the OR low, which sits just above the prior high of 2726.0 minus ~15 and near prev close), and has held there. The last bar closed 2718.1, up from the 2712.1 low. It is still above the 20-day average (2644.49), so the larger trend is up.

Entry: only on a reclaim, not now. Buy above ~2722 (the 09:30 bar high), ideally a 5-minute close back above 2726 (yesterday's high). Stop: below 2709, under the day low of 2711.2 and prev close. That's roughly 13-17 points of risk, less than one ATR (21.65), so it's tight and noise could hit it.

Target: VWAP at 2732.3, about 10-14 points away, which is under 1R. Realistically that's the only target; 2746 (the open) is a stretch.

Weaknesses: price is below VWAP, the index is down 0.93%, the day is -1.03%, volume is fading (122k down to 3k on the last partial bar), and relvol 3.56 was driven by the opening selling. Reward-to-risk is below 1 after costs. I would not take this unless it reclaims 2726 with volume.

Invalidation: any trade below 2711.2.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The Bull's own numbers sink the long. Reclaiming 2726 for a VWAP target at 2732.3 is under 1R, which costs turn into a loss. The "hold" at 2711.2 is one 3,142-share partial bar, so it proves nothing. The 20-DMA at 2644.49 is 74 points away and irrelevant intraday. The gap-up was rejected: 2776.5 high on the first bar, then a close at 2718.1, below the 2746.3 open, with VWAP at 2732.3 above price.

Bear case: the day is -1.03% with the index -0.93%, so this is not relative weakness, just beta. The opening range is 65 points wide (2776.5 to 2711.2), about 3 ATR, so the scanner's plan is poorly sized. Its stop of 2774.79 is 65 points away and the 2579.94 target is 130 points below, which is unrealistic. I would not use that plan.

Honest verdict: short only on a break, since price is just 6.9 points above the low. Trigger: a 5-minute close below 2711.2. Stop: 2732, at VWAP, about 21 points or 1 ATR. Target: 2690, about 1R, with yesterday's low 2673.4 as the stretch. Without a close below 2711.2, stay out, because the last bar's volume is too thin to read.

judge.title: ADANIENT: short on a break of the gap fill, stop at VWAP, target yesterday's low
judge.text: The gap-up was rejected. The stock opened at 2746.3, spiked to 2776.5 and sank to 2711.2. judge.title: No trade: COALINDIA: relative weakness is real, but the edge left is too thin to short
judge.text: The Bear wins on direction. Coal India is down 1.0% while the index is up 0.23%, it opened at its high of 403.0, and every bounce since (highs 399.55, 399.0, 398.95) has stalled at or below VWAP (399.065), so the Bull's long has no reclaim to stand on. Against a short, almost the whole 4.9-point opening range came in the first bar on 563k shares, and the last three bars have gone flat above 398.1, so a break below 397.9 would be chasing a move that is largely finished. A sensible stop at 399.7 risks 1.8 points, about one ATR5 (1.84), and the 395.0 target needs another 1.5 ATR of follow-through; once costs take roughly a quarter of the risk, that is a marginal edge, which by our rules is a loss. If forced to trade, it would be the short at 397.9, stop 399.7, target 395.0, but no trade is the better call.

cases.headline: Hero MotoCorp is drifting up with the market, but its first breakout try failed and buying has dried up, so stay out.
cases.bull:

It sits well above its 20-day average of 5270.4. Relative volume is 1.77, and the 09:20 bar, with 25,359 shares and a 5448.5 high, shows real buying. Price is 5438.0, above VWAP at 5432.9, and the index is up 0.23%, so it is not fighting the tape. The last bar, 09:30, closed at the high of the range on thin volume of 3,528.

Entry: the scanner's trigger of 5451.22 is only 13 points over the 5438 last price and just above the opening range high of 5448.5. I would wait for a 5-minute close above 5451 rather than anticipate it.

Stop: the plan puts it at 5399.0, about 52 points away, roughly 2 ATRs (ATR5 is 25.6). That is wide, so the size is about 9 shares for Rs 500 risk. A tighter stop below VWAP, around 5420, is arguably more logical.

Target: the plan's 5555.67 is about 104 points away, which is ambitious. I would aim for about 5500 realistically.

Wrong if: price closes below VWAP (5432.9), or the 5-minute bar falls back inside the range under 5420. Note that the 09:25 bar already rejected 5447, so the edge is thin after costs.
cases.bear:

The 5448.5 high on the 09:20 bar was the opening range top, and the 09:25 bar rejected 5447.0 and closed at 5422.0. That is a failed push, not clean buying. The Bull says the last bar closed at its high, but it is on 3,528 shares against 25,359 at the peak, so the volume is down about 86%. Price is only 5.1 points above VWAP, which is a small cushion. The Bull's tighter 5420 stop is under 1 ATR (25.6), so noise will likely hit it.

Short case: weak, and I would mostly stay out. The index is up 0.23%, which argues against fighting the tape. Still, there is a double-top feel near 5447-5448.5 on fading volume.

Conditional short: trigger on a 5-minute close below 5420, which is under the 09:25 low of 5420.0 and VWAP. Stop 5449. Target 5399. That is 21 points of reward for 29 of risk, a poor ratio after costs. My recommendation is to stay out.

judge.title: No trade: HEROMOTOCO: thin breakout edge, pass
judge.text: The long case has real support: price is 5438.0, just above VWAP at 5432.9; the day low of 5399.0 is above yesterday's high of 5393.5; relative volume is 1.77; and the index is up 0.23%. Against it, the 09:20 push to 5448.5 was rejected on the 09:25 bar, which closed at 5422.0. The bounce back to 5438 came on only 3,528 shares, against 25,359 on the peak bar, so buying is fading into the range top. The scanner's stop at 5399.0 is about 52 points (roughly 2 ATR) and its 5555.67 target is ambitious, while a tighter 5420 stop sits barely more than 1 ATR (25.6) away, so either version leaves a marginal edge that costs of about a quarter of the risk would erase. If forced to trade, I would go long on a break of 5451.5 with a stop at 5420 and a target of 5499, but the failed first test and drying volume make this a pass.

cases.headline: Britannia is sitting right on its morning low; a breakdown short is possible, but the reward barely covers costs, so we stay out.
cases.bull:
Honest case for a long is thin, and I'll say so up front.

The bull argument: price is sitting at 4723.9, right on the opening-range low of 4722.0 (it was defended twice, at 09:25 and 09:30, with lows of exactly 4722.0). That's a possible double-bottom. The 20-day average is 4730.09, so price is just under it, and the index is up 0.23% while BRITANNIA is down 0.76%, which leaves room for mean reversion. Selling volume is also fading: 8110, 5569, then 2075.

Entry: only on a confirmed bounce, say a 5-minute close above 4731 (reclaiming the 20DMA). The stop goes below 4722, around 4716, so risk is about 15 points, which keeps size workable. Realistic target: VWAP at 4744.8, about 14 points above entry. That's roughly 1R before costs, and costs eat about a quarter of that.

What proves me wrong: any 5-minute close below 4722. Also, the trend is down from the 4789.5 high, price is below VWAP, and relative volume of 1.75 favors sellers. Only four bars exist, so this is a weak setup. I'd pass unless the reclaim happens.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals: The double-bottom is two bars with identical lows of 4722.0, which is thin evidence, and the last bar's range (4722.0 to 4730.9) is only 8.9 points against an ATR of 25.8. That is compression, not a reversal. Fading volume (8110, 5569, 2075) shows selling exhaustion, but it also just reflects the usual opening burst fading. The 20DMA at 4730.09 is 6 points away, which is noise. Index up 0.23% while the stock is down 0.76% shows relative weakness, not a bounce signal. The Bull's target of 4744.8 is about 1R, and costs take a quarter of that, so the edge is marginal.

Short case: the stock reversed from 4789.5 to 4723.9, closing below the open (4760.3) and VWAP (4744.8). It opened near prev_close and failed under prev_hi of 4810.

But the scanner's plan is poor. Entry 4719.64 with a stop at 4789.5 risks about 70 points. The target of 4579.92 is 140 points away, about 5 ATRs, which is unrealistic. Only four bars exist.

My trade: short on a 5-minute close below 4722, entry about 4720. Stop 4745 (VWAP), 25 points risk. Target 4695, 1R. That is marginal after costs, so staying out is acceptable.

judge.title: No trade: BRITANNIA: OR-low breakdown short is too marginal, pass
judge.text: The bear side is the better side. The stock fell from 4789.5 to 4723.9, below VWAP (4744.8), below yesterday's low (4741.2) and below its 20DMA (4730.09). It is down 0.76% while the index is up 0.23%, and relative volume is 1.75. Even so, the trade does not pay: the scanner's 70-point stop and 140-point target (about 5 five-minute ATRs of 25.8) are unrealistic. A sensible VWAP stop of about 25 points allows only a roughly 1.5R target near 4681, and costs take about a quarter of R. The 4722.0 low has also held twice, and the last bar is a compressed 8.9-point range on fading volume (8110, 5569, 2075), so the breakdown could easily fail at support with only four bars of evidence. The bull's reclaim long gives about 1R into VWAP, which is worse, so neither side clears the cost hurdle and the verdict is NO_TRADE.

lessons.text: On longs, refusing is wrong when price sits 0% to 0.5% above VWAP and the stock is up less than about 2.3% so far, so take these. Pass on longs stretched more than 0.6% above VWAP or up more than 2.5% on the day, because the rule plan lost on all three such longs here, whatever the relative volume.

Favour shorts when the index is down and the stock is also down on the day: the rule plan made money in 6 of 6 such filled cases here, so do not refuse them. Pass on shorts when the index is up or the stock is green on the day: the rule plan lost or went flat in all four such cases.

last_review.summary: The Judge was right on moderate longs it took near VWAP (13) and on shorts taken with a falling index (8, 21), and it correctly refused shorts against a rising index or on a stock that was up (3, 7, 22). It refused too much: it passed five longs sitting just above VWAP that the rule plan made money on (0, 5, 11, 12) and one short in a down market (20), all at conviction 2. It lost on longs that were already stretched above VWAP or up a lot on the day (15, 23, 25), and its own tighter levels turned rule-plan winners into losses on two down-market shorts (18, 19).
